skill.name: higgsfield-faceless-video
skill.description: Create a finished faceless explainer, documentary, illustrated story or children's music video, or edit a previously created faceless video. Use when: "make a faceless video", "create a narrated explainer", "make a children's song video", "edit this faceless video". NOT for: a single silent clip, ads or UGC, unrelated footage edits, or script-only requests.
skill.summary: Create narrated videos, illustrated stories, and children's songs with Higgsfield generation and local assembly tools.
skill.author: higgsfield-ai

security_audit.summary: Of 365 static findings, 364 are false positives covering media tooling, temporary files, provenance checks, and documentation. One low-severity download risk remains because untrusted URLs and redirects can reach internal services. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious execution intent in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Asset downloads accept unrestricted destinations and follow redirects in scripts/assemble_blocks.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Validate resolved destinations before each request and redirect; reject private, loopback, and link-local addresses unless explicitly authorized. Add download time and size limits.

content.value_statement: Producing narrated videos requires coordinated scripts, visuals, audio, and timing. This skill guides Higgsfield generation and local assembly with checks before delivery.
actual_capabilities: Plan and generate narrated explainers, documentaries, and stories through the Higgsfield CLI.
Assemble ordered motion clips and narration with speech timing, audio coverage, duration, and decode checks.
Build picture story timelines from local transcription and bind image job receipts to ordered frames.
Guide creation and assembly of 60-second or 120-second children's song videos.
Align authored narration to local transcription, export SRT subtitles, and burn captions into video.
Replace selected 10-second video ranges or composite an explicitly requested, authorized presenter.
limitations: Generation requires a configured Higgsfield account, available models, paid credits, and local media tools.
Captioning and picture stories require faster-whisper and an existing local transcription model; singing captions are unsupported.
Song mode supports only 60 or 120 seconds; partial edits require ordered, non-overlapping 10-second grid ranges.
Generated facts, identities, wording, and synchronization require human review; technical receipts do not guarantee content accuracy.

use_cases.title: Illustrate a lesson
use_cases.description: Create a narrated science explainer with diagram-led scenes, a consistent voice, and optional subtitles.

use_cases.title: Produce a documentary episode
use_cases.description: Plan sourced narration, recurring visual references, and ordered motion blocks for a channel episode.

use_cases.title: Create an original children's song
use_cases.description: Develop a supported-length song and matching illustrated scenes with consistent characters and a repeating chorus.

prompt_templates.title: Create a short explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-second faceless explainer about how rain forms, in English and 16:9. Use illustrated diagrams, one narrator, and no music or subtitles. Show available voices and estimated costs before generation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a narrated picture story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 60-second picture story about a seed becoming a tree, in English and 9:16. Use storybook images, continuous narration, and subtitles. Verify local transcription prerequisites before paid generation and align scenes to the completed narration.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a sourced channel episode
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-second channel-style motion episode about early navigation, in English and 16:9. Use reliable sources, a recurring ship reference, varied shots, and one narrator. Validate the script, measure narration takes, and assemble only after all checks pass. Retain job receipts for recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Revise selected video ranges
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit my previously generated 60-second faceless video using the supplied source and project assets. Replace only 10-20 seconds and 40-50 seconds with the supplied corrections. Preserve all other content and the existing style and voice. Validate patch ranges and replacement media, then assemble a full-length review draft. Do not upload or publish it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: targeted edits to an existing production

output_examples.input: A 15-second English explainer with two illustrated scenes and no subtitles.
output: Expected deliverable: one assembled video with a 10-second opening block and a 5-second final block.
Supporting artifacts: a poster image and an assembly receipt with per-block speech timing.
Delivery note: measured duration, aspect ratio, language, subtitle status, and factual sources when applicable.

output_examples.input: Replace the middle 10-second range of a previously generated 30-second video.
output: Expected deliverable: a full-length review draft containing the replacement scene and surrounding source content.
Supporting artifact: an assembly receipt listing the edited range and measured output duration.
Review requirement: compare the edited range and surrounding content before publication.

best_practices: Confirm duration, aspect ratio, voice, image roles, subtitle prerequisites, and generation costs before paid work.
Save job IDs, returned URLs, completed assets, scripts, and receipts in a persistent session directory.
Use trusted asset URLs and review the first scene, failed timing checks, captions, and final video before delivery.
anti_patterns: Speeding up narration or bypassing failed assembly checks to force a finished result.
Regenerating completed assets or submitting duplicate jobs while an earlier generation is still running.
Treating an incidental photo as presenter authorization or uploading a review draft without a request.

faq.question: Does the skill include free video generation?
faq.answer: No. It uses Higgsfield generation services and requires account access, available models, and credits. It checks estimated costs where supported.

faq.question: Which local tools are required?
faq.answer: Core workflows use Bash, FFmpeg, ffprobe, Python 3, curl, and awk. Presenter processing also uses NumPy and Pillow.

faq.question: Is narration sent to an external transcription service?
faq.answer: Caption transcription runs locally with faster-whisper and an existing model. Video, voice, and image generation still use Higgsfield services.

faq.question: Can it create songs at any duration?
faq.answer: No. Song mode supports only 60 or 120 seconds. It does not support captions for singing.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing faceless video?
faq.answer: Yes. It replaces selected, ordered, non-overlapping 10-second ranges and produces a full-length review draft. Other editing tasks are outside its scope.

faq.question: Does it publish completed videos automatically?
faq.answer: No. Hosted delivery requires a request and uses the confirmed upload URL. Edited videos remain review drafts and must not be published automatically.
